soil-found-085.title: Lichens, microbes and the first bite into bare rock
soil-found-085.text: Bare rock starts becoming soil when living things attack it with acid. The first colonizers, such as lichens, mosses and microbes, begin the work. Lichens and other microorganisms, including cyanobacteria, green algae, fungi and bacteria, secrete oxalic acid. Lichens have long been seen as the pioneers of soil. Seed-bearing plants can colonize faster, but lichens tolerate harsher conditions and dominate in alpine regions. Organic acids from roots and decay, such as citric and phenolic acids, {{ref:soil-chem-059}} and {{ref:soil-chem-060}}, speed chemical breakdown by gripping metal atoms and pulling them from minerals. As the soil thickens, earthworms, burrowing mammals and large animals above ground go on altering its chemistry and fertility.
